communication.description: Generic interaction patterns between a person and an agent, and between an orchestrating agent and its sub-agents.

core.description: Skills that teach an agent about sous itself: what sous manages, how its configuration works, how templates render, and how skills are written. Auto-subscribed in every project, with opt-out-only semantics.

tool-usage.description: Recipes that teach an agent to drive an external tool, together with the scripts and references that tool needs.

workflow.description: Task tracking, branch conventions and issue-board practice: the recipes that shape how a unit of work starts, is recorded, and finishes.

communication/control-flow.description: Generic interaction skills for steering a session: approve a plan and proceed, ask for an opinion without acting, repeat the last instruction, and run a research task across background sub-agents.

core/sous-skills.description: The skills that teach an agent what sous is and how it works: which files sous owns and must never be hand-edited, how a sous configuration is written and debugged, the .tpl. template convention and LiquidJS syntax, what an agent skill is, and how to create one.

tool-usage/automated-browser-tasks.description: Headless browser automation driven from the user's own Chrome session: the ctx API, the auth and cookie model, the scriptwriting conventions, and skills for writing, updating and running a browser task.

workflow/github-projects.description: The GitHub Issues and Projects v2 workflow: how issues are written, picked up, moved across a board's Status column, and closed, with action skills for creating an issue, picking one to work on, and filing tech debt.

workflow/sub-agent-delegation.description: The orchestrator-and-sub-agent working pattern that the other recipes cite: the main session reasons, decides and talks to the user, and delegates execution to background sub-agents.

workflow/task-files.description: Per-branch task files: one working-notes file per git branch, with skills for starting a task, resuming one, updating it before a session ends, and carrying remaining work into a follow-up branch.
